tagline: Democratizing global investing through social trading and education
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of Funded Accounts (3.81 million as of December 31, 2025) represents the core of eToro's business model. These active and funded accounts are the direct source of Net Contribution and reflect the company's ability to acquire, convert, and retain retail users across its key markets in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Americas.

kpis.name: Active funded accounts
kpis.explanation: Users who have completed KYC/AML, activated their account, deposited funds, executed at least one transaction, and maintain a positive balance.
kpis.description: As of December 31, 2025, eToro had 3.81 million Funded Accounts, up from 3.48 million as of December 31, 2024. This metric represents the most engaged users who generate Net Contribution.
kpis.signal: Consistent growth in monetizable user base since Q1 2023

kpis.name: Net contribution
kpis.explanation: Total revenue and income less cost of revenue from cryptoassets and margin interest expense. Key metric to evaluate net contribution before overhead costs.
kpis.description: For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, Net Contribution was USD 227 million, down compared to USD 252 million in Q4 2024, but up 4.6% on average annually (227M vs 217M in Q1 2025).
kpis.signal: Quarterly volatility tied to market conditions and retail investor sentiment

kpis.name: Total annual trades
kpis.explanation: Total number of orders executed by users covering traditional assets and cryptoassets.
kpis.description: For 2025, users executed 594 million trades, up from 571 million in 2024 and 446 million in 2023. Trades in stocks, commodities, and currencies represented 537 million, while cryptoassets accounted for 57 million.
kpis.signal: Sustained enthusiasm from retail investors for global markets and cryptoassets

risks.title: Dependence on market volatility and unpredictable fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Major risk positioned first in Item 1A, highly intensive language ("significantly fluctuate", "unpredictable"), stable but structural trend to the activity. High category weight: direct impact on trading volumes, number of funded accounts, and revenue.

risks.title: Risks of losses from extreme market movements and risk management
risks.score_rationale: Second major detailed risk, highly intensive language ("abrupt and erratic", "unable to execute"), stable trend. Critical impact: eToro operates primarily as principal and holds positions exposed to price fluctuations, counterparty default, and liquidity risks.

risks.title: Intense competition from traditional and fintech players across all segments
risks.score_rationale: Major detailed risk at end of section, intensive language ("highly competitive", "expect competition to further intensify"), upward trend. High category weight: direct threat to user retention and market share against banks, neobanks, tech brokers, and crypto exchanges.

risks.title: Risk of user and counterparty default during periods of volatility
risks.score_rationale: Specific detailed risk, moderate to intensive language ("increased risk of default"), stable trend but aggravated by economic turbulence. Material impact: leveraged users may fail to meet obligations, creating cascade default risk.

risks.title: User dissatisfaction, disputes, and reputational damage
risks.score_rationale: Major detailed risk, intensive language ("highly susceptible", "severely negatively impacted"), stable trend. High category weight: social nature of platform amplifies negative complaints and can cause user loss and trading volume decline.

risks.title: Cybersecurity, personal data, and GDPR/CCPA compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in forward-looking statements and user retention factors, moderate language ("cybersecurity incidents"), stable but increasing trend. Material impact: loss of user assets, data breaches, regulatory fines, and loss of trust.

risks.title: Regulatory and legal framework changes across multiple jurisdictions
risks.score_rationale: Major risk mentioned in forward-looking statements and retention factors, intensive language ("changes in regulatory and legal framework", "regulatory inquiries"), upward trend. High category weight: eToro operates in multiple jurisdictions with divergent regulations (MiCA, DSA, FCA, CySEC, CFTC).

risks.title: Dependence on user growth and market saturation risk
risks.score_rationale: Major detailed risk, intensive language ("failure to retain existing users or add new users"), stable trend. Material impact: user growth is key driver of revenue; saturation or decline directly affects business model viability.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or AI capabilities in provided documents. eToro does not position AI as a strategic lever in recent communications. Focus remains on user collaboration, financial education, and simplified multi-asset access.
